instructions: For each pending route, exercise every applicable state and viewport below with realistic long and empty values. Record source and browser-test evidence before changing status to reviewed. Retain necessary authorization, provenance, consequence, and validation information.

problems: The full destination list required unnecessary scanning
Group relationships were labels rather than operable structure
shared_surfaces.correction: Keep every direct link in five task-based groups; use accessible disclosure headings; persist browser choices; reveal the active destination; retain a single-level mobile menu.

problems: Spacing, corner, control-height, width, and shadow values were repeated without a shared contract
The shared stylesheet referenced accent and shadow variables that were not defined
A fixed page-header minimum height and generous panel spacing created avoidable dead space
shared_surfaces.correction: Use the documented compact token scale for the application frame, page hierarchy, reusable actions, forms, dialogs, messages, empty states, and filter menus; reserve restrained shadows for overlays; retain focus, forced-colors, reduced-motion, mobile, and print behavior.

problems: Authentication and portal shells bypassed the shared spacing, control, and width tokens
The client portal referenced undefined surface and semantic-color variables
Client invoice state used a decorative pill and the portal lacked a keyboard skip link
shared_surfaces.correction: Use the compact shared foundations for setup, sign-in, MFA, recovery, account security, and the client portal; keep security consequences and recovery guidance explicit; render portal lifecycle state as plain text; provide a skip link; stack long portal rows at narrow widths.

problems: Organization overview repeated the navigation inventory below the organization facts and relationships
The MSP overview still reports every supported area as Available instead of summarizing useful workspace activity
routes.correction: Removed the duplicate organization-area list; retain the direct organization profile, external ticket state, and relationships. The MSP overview requires a later activity-oriented correction before this route is complete.

problems: The type filter used a standalone select while other list filters use one recognizable filter menu
routes.correction: Kept New organization as the sole primary page action and moved organization type into the shared filter menu; retained direct row-level Edit and Archive actions because both are common and unambiguous.

problems: Search, field selection, filter value, and column settings were four equally prominent toolbar controls
The two-part field filter bypassed the standard filter treatment
routes.correction: Kept search visible, combined field and value inside the shared filter menu, and left column selection as a distinct table-view preference; retained one primary create action and compact row actions.

problems: Every site exposed four equally weighted actions and every nested location exposed three, overwhelming the hierarchy
routes.correction: Kept Add location visible as the site row's common action and moved custom fields, edit, and archive into clearly labelled overflow menus; nested locations use the same compact menu.

routes.focus: documents, editor, settings, structured types, reuse, review, publication, PDF and export
problems: The sticky reader toolbar used blur, translucency, a full border, and rounded floating-panel styling
The document surface has several editing, publication, history, key, file, export, and settings states still requiring individual review
routes.correction: Changed the reader toolbar to an opaque, square-edged work bar with one separating rule. Continue the route state-by-state before marking it reviewed.

No structural correction required: the route uses one visible search field, a semantic file table, a direct owning-document link, and one row-level Download action with truthful loading, error, empty, and no-match states.

problems: New asset opened below the complete master-detail inventory, so the initiating action could appear to do nothing
Lifecycle, retained-document, batch, and relationship states still require narrow-screen browser review
routes.correction: Moved the new-asset editor directly below the page header, focused its model search, and identified its search control semantically. Retained explicit review-before-archive behavior for batch actions.

problems: New and edit forms appeared after the complete license master-detail view
Assignment, linking, and long history states still require narrow-screen browser review
routes.correction: Placed new and edit forms directly under the page action and error area, with focus in the license-name field; retained contextual seat and installation actions in the selected record.

problems: The network editor opened below the record table and relationship map
An initial network-service failure remained visually stuck on Loading
Different DNS editors could remain open together
The relationship canvas and saved-view controls still require responsive browser review
routes.correction: Moved the network editor directly below its page action, focused the first field, made record searches semantic, gave row edit actions record-specific names, surfaced initial service failures, and limited service editing to one form at a time.

problems: Monitoring history, endpoint history, and long evidence values still require responsive browser review
routes.correction: Source review confirmed one primary add action, an adjacent focused form, one contextual details action per row, explicit loading and empty states, and horizontally bounded evidence tables.

problems: Long endpoint and validation histories still require responsive browser review
routes.correction: Source review confirmed a visible domain search, contextual endpoint creation and checking, explicit pending and empty states, and bounded history tables without competing page-level actions.

problems: New and edit forms appeared after the complete credential-link list
The visible link search was not identified as a search input
routes.correction: Moved the credential-link form directly below its page action, focused the title field, made search semantic, and retained the explicit boundary that TekDocs stores references rather than secrets.

problems: Archive contract and remove cost changed retained records immediately, without presenting the consequence for confirmation
Cost visibility, long values, and dialogs still require responsive browser review
routes.correction: Added explicit, cancelable confirmation for contract archive and cost removal, described each consequence in plain language, focused the first field in contract and cost dialogs, and kept financial values permission-controlled.

problems: Long supplier names and websites still require responsive browser review
routes.correction: Source review found no unnecessary actions or decorative containers: the route is a derived, read-only supplier list with explicit loading, unavailable, and empty states.

problems: New product opened below the product catalog and specification-template sections
Model, template, archive, and long-specification states still require responsive browser review
routes.correction: Moved new-product creation directly below the product/template switcher, focused the product name, identified product search semantically, and retained consequence-first confirmation for archive and document removal.

routes.focus: draft, line items, issuance, delivery, lifecycle and handoff
stock, provenance, quantity history and invoice use
controls, evidence, risks, reviews and bundles
connections, sync, observations, conflicts, stale state and recovery
results, filters, excerpts and no-result state
sessions, MFA, tokens and destructive actions
service state and technical detail hierarchy
documents, files, invoices, withdrawn, denied and failure
safe result and recovery without feature advertising
